hook.text: A grassroots movement demands policy change. Millions support it online. But it was created by a PR firm.

buildup.text: Astroturfing means fake grassroots campaigns. Corporations and governments hire firms to simulate public demand.

discovery.text: Tobacco companies pioneered this offline. Social media made it cheap and scalable. One firm can fake a movement.

twist.text: Real grassroots movements get accused of astroturfing too. The tactic poisons trust in all collective action.

climax.text: Researchers found astroturfing in climate debates, vaccine discussions, and trade policy—on every side.

punchline.text: Not every crowd is a community. Some are products.

quiz.question: What is astroturfing?
options: Fake grassroots campaigns funded by organizations
A type of social media algorithm
